body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1: 1.8.1 is already deployed, this is for the next
release.

## Problem

One authenticated member can wedge every WRITE on the instance for ~12 s per
request, repeatably.

The 4 MB MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH admits ~38,900 minimal item rows (measured: 108
bytes/row). apply_changes costs ~0.31 ms/row, and the SQLite write transaction
is held from the first _bump() until conn.commit() at routes/sync.py:81 — so the
write lock is held for the whole apply loop.

db.py:39 uses stock sqlite3.connect(), i.e. a 5000 ms busy timeout, and
OperationalError is unhandled. Measured against a held write transaction:

    login    during that window -> HTTP 500 after 5.2 s
    register during that window -> HTTP 500
    GET registration-status     -> HTTP 200   (WAL keeps reads alive)

So a single large /sync 500s every login, registration, sync and settings write
instance-wide. Reads are unaffected (WAL).

Secondary: name_merge() rescans all live items of every touched list on every
sync. Measured: a 1-item push into a 7,500-item list already costs 66 ms, and
that cost is permanent once a list is large.

## Fix

Server:
- Cap rows per /sync batch. MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is the wrong lever — it bounds
  bytes, not work. Reject over-cap batches with a 422 carrying a distinct error
  code so clients can react (and so it is distinguishable from 413).
- User's constraint: the cap must be AT LEAST 50 rows/sync. Note the measured
  cost when picking the actual value — 50 rows is ~15 ms, 250 rows ~78 ms, so a
  value in the low hundreds is comfortably safe and costs far fewer round trips
  on a large initial sync. 50 is the floor, not necessarily the value.
- Pass an explicit timeout= to sqlite3.connect() and handle OperationalError
  ("database is locked") as a 503 with Retry-After rather than an unhandled 500.

Clients (web + android) — MUST ship together with the server cap, or an
over-cap push starts failing with a 422 instead of succeeding:
- Split larger pending-change sets into chunks at or below the server cap and
  push them sequentially.
- Chunking must be resumable: a failed chunk must not lose or double-apply the
  remaining queue. Field-level LWW makes re-pushing a chunk safe, so retry the
  failed chunk rather than restarting the batch.

## Verification

- A batch one row over the cap is rejected with the new code; a batch at the cap
  succeeds.
- A client with (cap + N) pending changes converges in multiple round trips.
- Concurrent writers during a slow write get 503, not 500.
title: sync: cap rows per batch + chunk on clients; one large /sync 500s all writes instance-wide
